correctness.rationale: For a finite split basic algebra, generation modulo J² lifts to generation of A by nilpotence; a square-zero S-bimodule split gives independent vertex labels in F_q^r, whose all-distinct probability is (q^r)_v/q^(rv). For each loop arrow block r uniform directions remain and for each off-diagonal block conjugating the semisimple complement removes exactly one common vertex-difference direction, giving beta_q(m_ii,r) and beta_q(m_ij,r-1). The factors multiply across blocks; higher radical relations vanish. A separately enumerated 2×2 triangular F2 example has 24 generating ordered pairs out of 64, agreeing with 3/8. For v=q^k,r=2k+t, the collision exponent is -q^-t/2 and sparse bounded-multiplicity rank failures sum O(q^-k). The small enumeration is corroboration, not an all-q proof.
